我认为在客户和市场研究方面，你需要找一个有用户研究背景但注重流程导向的人。所以我会寻找既懂用户研究代码，又精通相关策略的人——这些技能能帮助他们搭建工具包，选择合适的原型设计和可用性测试软件。他们要清楚高质量访谈的标准，还要有持续优化流程的意愿。比如他们会说：“我需要建立一个系统来解决这个问题。”这种善于将想法付诸实践的能力对每个人都很重要。他们会说：“我能开发一个系统来修复这个问题。”这其实是一个很棒的面试问题，我建议产品运营人员可以用这个问题。我从未想到过，但可以这样问：“请分享你在工作中遇到过的最让人头疼的流程或问题，最后你是如何通过自动化或搭建系统来优化它的。” 我认为这对任何相关职位都是绝佳的面试题。

（00:55:27）关于用户和市场洞察方面的职位，虽然目前从事这方面工作的人不多，但研究运营领域正在兴起，我认为这对我们很有价值。比如Fidelity的案例研究对象Jen Cardello，她负责用户洞察团队，同时也是该团队的副总裁。她不仅管理用户研究员，还领导研究运营团队。研究运营团队负责建立参与者数据库，开发用户研究工具包，并为其他人提供优质的用户研究培训。

（00:56:07）由于合规原因，Jen的团队成员无法直接与客户和金融机构接触。他们通过认证确保研究人员在特定范围内开展工作，设定不同权限级别以实现研究民主化。若研究项目存在合规问题，团队会提交给Jen的团队，由用户研究员协助完成。

（00:56:33）关键在于如何处理合规问题。比如，关于向客户透露信息的限制，以及问卷设计的规范，他们需要巧妙应对这些复杂问题。Jen来自研究运营背景，拥有完整的用户体验经验，但研究运营是她的专长，她在Athenahealth和Fidelity都表现出色。

（00:57:00）如果能找到具备相关背景的人，那再好不过。但若找不到Jen这样的人才，至少要确保候选人有用户研究背景，可能还需具备用户体验经验。他们要善于将研究成果转化为可执行的方案。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Jen's about to get a bunch of LinkedIn requests too.
turns.zh: Jen又要收到一堆领英请求了。

turns.speaker: Melissa Perri
turns.en: Sorry for your inbox, Jen.
turns.zh: Jen，真是麻烦你了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I feel like the research team is going to hate people now for pulling you into product ops. Who would you suggest product ops report to generally at least to start?
turns.zh: 我感觉研发团队现在会因为你把他拉进产品运营部门而对他心存不满。你觉得产品运营部门通常应该向谁汇报？至少在初期阶段应该向谁汇报？

turns.speaker: Melissa Perri
turns.en: Head a product.
turns.zh: 向产品负责人汇报。

turns.speaker: Denise Tilles
turns.en: CPO.
turns.zh: 首席产品官（CPO）。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Such a clear, quick answer. I love it. How do they find time to train and work with this person? Are they the right-hand person that helps them just make everything more efficient? What's a way? What's that relationship like?
turns.zh: 回答得如此清晰、简洁。我太喜欢了。他们怎么有时间培训和指导这个人？他们是首席产品官的得力助手吗？帮助他们提高效率吗？具体怎么做？这种关系是怎样的？

turns.speaker: Melissa Perri
turns.en: I think definitely their right-hand person, and we say to a lot of CPOs, especially high growth companies, "Make your first hire just a product ops person to help you get this data out and start looking at it," because that helps them with board meetings, it helps them set strategy. Usually when you walk into a growth stage company, that's the first thing that you need to do is make sure that it's working, that you need to set it. Typically, when you're getting hired, there's usually a strategy problem and that person, they're like your right-hand man trying to operationalize that. So I definitely think that you're going to be guiding them there. (00:58:23): I think this comes back to our question though about, do you hire somebody with experience or do you hire somebody who's new to it? If you as a CPO don't have a lot of time to train up somebody on product ops because you've got 8,000 fires to fight, then hire somebody with experience who knows how to do it and operationalize it. If you are like, "My biggest issue is business data and insights," for example, "and I just need to get my data so that I can do the strategy pieces and then I need to think through and work through what I want product ops to look like," maybe then you just hire the data analyst. If they're confident in the data analysis piece, it's pretty easy, I haven't done this myself, to teach them about what types of information you need to see as a product person. They're going to need a lot more handholding at the beginning because they're not going to know all the different cuts of data, but it's not an investment of an inordinate amount of time to be able to get something valuable back. (00:59:20): It's not like training for 40 hours a week and then waiting six months to see results. It's more about, "I need you to go pull these types of cuts. Here's why. Let me explain to you this so that you learn it and then you can think about it next time," but that's going to help you there too. So I think it really depends. So how fast you need product ops fully rolled out and then how much time you have to train people, and then where you're starting from there and how big and how much buy-in you have to grow this thing from the get-go.
turns.zh: 我觉得他肯定是首席产品官的得力助手。我们常对很多CPO，尤其是高增长公司说：“首位招聘的产品运营人员，要帮助你提取数据并开始分析。”因为这能助力董事会会议，助力战略制定。通常进入成长阶段的公司，首要任务就是确保数据系统正常运作并进行优化。刚入职时，公司往往面临战略问题，而这个人就像你的得力助手，帮助你将战略落地。（00:58:23）不过这又回到了我们的问题：是招聘有经验的人，还是新手？如果CPO没有时间培训产品运营人员，因为日常工作繁忙，那就直接招聘有经验的人，让他们快速上手。如果你面临的主要问题是商业数据和洞察，比如“我需要获取数据以制定战略”，然后再思考产品运营部门的架构，或许可以先招聘数据分析师。如果他们对数据分析有信心，教他们产品视角需要关注的数据类型并不难。初期他们需要更多手把手指导，因为他们不熟悉各种数据维度，但投入适度时间就能获得宝贵成果。（00:59:20）这不是每周培训40小时然后等半年才见效，而是逐步引导：“现在去提取这些数据。原因是这样的。让我解释一下，这样你就能掌握，然后下次再优化。”这也会助你一臂之力。所以关键在于：你需要多快让产品运营部门全面运转起来，培训时间有多少，初始基础如何，以及从一开始就获得多大的支持和认可。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome. Maybe as a last question, I'd love to go through a quick case study of a company you worked with and just share maybe how you rolled it out, what you ran into, challenges you had to overcome, and maybe the benefits and impact that adding this role had.
turns.zh: 太棒了。最后一个问题，我想快速分享一个你合作过的公司的案例，讲讲如何推进、遇到的挑战、克服的难题，以及这个角色带来的益处和影响。

turns.speaker: Melissa Perri
turns.en: When I was at Athenahealth, we were doing a ... Athenahealth has always been a software company, so let me put it that way, but they didn't have a formal product management role and they had just implemented it when I came in. So the chief product officer brought me in. He did not have an extensive product background, so he said, "I need to train all these product people and figure out what to do with this organization." So I came in to help him do that. We had over 360 product managers. We had 5,000 software developers there and it was a massive platform, $8 billion in market cap, I think, electronic health record system. (01:00:42): So this is where I started to realize we needed product ops. This was me discovering this. So I'll tell you how we rolled it out and probably what we would do differently next time, but we had trained all the product managers. People were starting to use a lot of the things that we were teaching, and we saw that the maturity was getting a lot better in the organization, which was fantastic, but then we started to run into these problems, and these problems that we found could not be solved by just training product managers, and that's where the concept for product ops came up. (01:01:11): We also realized we had way too many product managers, just way too many product managers. There was one person reporting into one person all the way down, and we were like, "This is not helpful." So we ended up training everybody, teaching people about what the role was, and then thinking through as we encounter these other problems, "What else do we need besides product managers?" Product ops became one of the things. We also had people actually move out of product management into other roles. We had people become data analysts, we had people become user researchers, we had people go into other parts of the organization, but a lot of people after we trained them actually just self-selected out of product management and some of them did come to us and say, "What else is there?" (01:01:53): When we looked at the product ops role, we said, "Okay. What are the big fires that we have to fight that's just not from a lack of skills perspective?" That's a big part about product ops. It's not a replacement for product managers or product leaders not having product management skills. It's to help skilled product managers and product leaders do their job better. So this will never replace the fact that people don't have the skills to do their job. (01:02:19): So where we ran into issues was, one, getting insights back to the executives on what the teams were actually doing. So the CEO and I were sitting there trying to set strategy and set the vision for the company and I was helping him formulate it into written form and help him deploy it and think through where we want it to go. He was in Jira, digging around in Jira trying to find information on what people were working on, and I was like, "You're not going to find that in Jira, especially when we've got hundreds of thousands of tickets for 5,000 people. You're not going to find this in there." (01:02:57): That started to show me, "Hey, he's looking for this. What do you want to see?" He's looking for a portfolio roadmap of what everybody's doing and he wanted to see what are the big pushes we're making from a feature perspective and how do they tie back to our overall strategy and our goals. What's going to help our retention? What's going to help us get new customers? What's going to help us move into the enterprise, which was a big thing we were doing going upmarket into hospitals? We had no transparency into the allocation of R&D on that and also the roadmaps on that. (01:03:29): So one of the things that we were trying to do in product ops was build that view, try to figure out how we get people to put the right information into Jira at the right level. So we actually had to train people on how to write ... At the time, we only had Jira, so epics in Jira that were not just build a button, they were more substantial than that. They actually had to meet behind it so we could look at it. Then we had to go out and find the right software to roll that up into a portfolio view so the executives could get the insights they were looking for. (01:04:00): We also had to build a way to track the OKRs that were deployed and actually see where it was. So we had to build the dashboards for that. So we started there and that became really important because that was a big issue was just the executive visibility, how do we make consistent roadmaps across the organizations, how do we get visibility into what's going on. As we started to identify more and more things, we said, "We're a huge team. We should actually have somebody overseeing this." (01:04:27): Data and insights was a really big issue in the company in general, and we knew we had to instrument things better, and at the time, they brought in Amplitude and they were starting to put an Amplitude everywhere in the organization, but it wasn't fully rolled out yet. So we had these people who were going around trying to help the individual product teams get the information out of Amplitude and we said, "We need this to be more of a consistent thing, a consistent program." (01:04:52): So that sparked the need for having our first product operations leader. So we ended up creating a VP of product operations and somebody moved from the product management role into that. She was much more of a process type person. She wanted to really help arm the teams into being able to get good data out there, but she understood product management well enough where she knew how all this stuff worked and she wanted to create the systems internally. (01:05:17): So reporting into her, we had a business data and insights team that was overseeing Amplitude rollout and they were also putting people around the director level overseeing usually five to let's say eight Scrum teams on the director level, sometimes smaller just depending on the product. We had a business data and insights person embedded at that level to help get the ad hoc reports out now because we weren't well-instrumented. We said, "We're still making the programs and the shared services at the top level, but these people need to make decisions today. So how do we get them to do that?" So she oversaw that team. She had somebody directed there. (01:05:55): then we also had the people looking at the portfolio views and the governance and the rollout and the rollout of that getting put into that as well. So that helped us get going with that. On the other side, so this didn't fall under product operations at the time, but like I said, Jen Cardello was doing research ops there and leading this team around the user insights. She got the participant database out. That was fantastic. She got out a bunch of different user research tools. They made a design systems database too that helped us be able to do prototyping a lot faster and have consistent design processes, which was amazing. (01:06:32): The head of UX reported into the chief product officer. So it still fell under the CPO, but it reported into the head of UX on that side and that was totally fine because we just collaborated with them pretty much all the time. So that's how we started to roll it out and get going and that's where that need was and it became so much better to get the insights that we needed out there. (01:06:53): Then what happened was, actually, Athenahealth at this time, it was really wild and private. So this is where I left and a lot of leaders left at the same time, but they ended up restructuring it and they actually kept the product ops team. So now, Tim Davenport oversees product ops team. He was the chief of staff for the chief product officer at the time and he's been building it, again, taking the stuff that worked and then building onto it, and they're actually one of our key studies in the book as well about what Tim's doing now and how he's orchestrated as well to help with opex and capex and accounting type issues that they were having too. (01:07:28): So Athenahealth has been through many different restructurings since I've been there, but they have always kept product ops and their current chief product officer said that he will never go anywhere else that doesn't have product ops. That's how much he believes in it.
turns.zh:
我在Athenahealth工作时，我们当时正在做一个……Athenahealth一直是一家软件公司，所以这么说吧，但他们当时并没有正式的产品管理职位，我加入后他们才刚刚设立这个职位。于是首席产品官找我加入。他本身没有深厚的产品背景，所以他说：“我需要培训所有产品团队成员，规划如何运作整个组织。”于是我来帮助他做这件事。我们当时有超过360名产品经理，还有5000名软件开发人员，平台规模庞大，市值约80亿美元，属于电子健康记录系统。（01:00:42）：就在这时，我开始意识到我们需要产品运营团队。这是我对此的发现。我会讲讲我们是如何推行产品运营的，或许还能谈谈下次会如何改进，但我们确实培训了所有产品经理。人们开始应用我们传授的许多方法，组织的成熟度明显提升，这很棒，但随后我们遇到了一些问题，这些问题仅靠培训产品经理无法解决，产品运营的概念由此产生。（01:01:11）：我们还意识到产品经理数量过多，太多太多了。从上到下每个人都只对一个人汇报，我们觉得这毫无帮助。于是我们最终对所有人进行培训，教他们理解产品经理的角色，然后在遇到其他问题时思考：“除了产品经理，我们还需要什么？” 产品运营团队就是其中一项。我们甚至有一些人从产品管理岗位转向其他角色，比如成为数据分析师、用户研究员，或者进入组织的其他部门。但许多接受培训后的人最终主动退出产品管理领域，有些人确实来问：“还有其他机会吗？” （01:01:53）：审视产品运营角色时，我们问：“好吧，我们需要应对哪些迫在眉睫的挑战？” 这正是产品运营的核心所在。它并非取代产品经理或产品领导的技能缺失，而是帮助有能力的管理者更好地开展工作。因此，它永远无法替代那些缺乏技能的人。 （01:02:19）：我们遇到的难题之一是，向高管汇报团队实际进展情况。我们和CEO坐在一起，试图制定公司战略和愿景。我帮他将其转化为书面文件，协助部署并思考未来方向。他却在Jira系统里翻找信息，试图了解团队在做什么。我说：“你别在Jira里找了，尤其是我们有5000名员工，数十万个工单。你找不到的。” （01:02:57）：这让我意识到：“他在找什么？” 他需要一份产品路线图，了解每个人在做什么项目，从功能角度看哪些是重头戏，又如何与我们的整体战略和目标相结合。哪些能提升用户留存率？哪些能帮助我们赢得新客户？哪些能助力我们进军企业级市场？这正是我们向高端市场进军的关键举措。
医院？我们对研发资源分配和路线图规划缺乏透明度。（01:03:29）：因此，产品运营团队试图建立这样的视图，引导团队将正确的信息以合适的层级录入Jira系统。当时我们仅有Jira平台，因此Jira中的“Epic”任务不只是“构建按钮”那么简单，而是需要更深入的规划。为此，我们必须召开专题会议进行讨论。随后，我们需要寻找合适的软件将这些信息整合成项目组合视图，以便高管们获取所需洞察。（01:04:00）：此外，我们还需追踪已部署的OKR进展并实时掌握执行情况。因此，我们专门搭建了相关仪表盘。这些基础工作的确至关重要，因为高管层对项目进展的把控能力，以及各部门路线图的统一性，都曾成为关键挑战。随着问题逐渐浮出水面，我们意识到团队规模庞大，急需设立专门职位进行统筹管理。（01:04:27）：数据与洞察力是公司整体面临的重大挑战。我们深知必须优化数据采集体系，当时公司已引入Amplitude分析平台并开始在全公司推广，但系统尚未全面上线。因此，我们组织团队成员协助各产品团队从Amplitude中提取数据，并计划将这项工作提升为系统化项目。（01:05:17）：最终，我们设立了首位产品运营副总裁一职，并从产品管理岗位调派人员担任此职。她更偏向流程型思维，既能为团队提供数据支持，又深谙产品管理逻辑，善于搭建内部数据体系。（01:05:55）：在她的领导下，商业数据与洞察团队负责Amplitude平台的推广，并派遣副总监级别人员管理5-8个Scrum团队，视具体产品规模而定。团队配备专业人员协助处理临时报告需求，因为当时数据采集体系尚不完善。我们需要确保高层决策层面与基层团队之间的信息流转顺畅。（01:06:32）：此外，用户洞察团队（当时隶属于产品运营）在Jen Cardello的领导下开展工作，成功搭建参与者数据库，整合多款用户研究工具，并建立设计系统数据库，这些举措极大提升了原型设计效率，推动了设计标准化进程，成效显著。（01:07:03）：用户体验部门直接向首席产品官汇报，保持了与CPO的职能对接，但具体工作由用户体验负责人统筹管理。

---
另一方面，这完全没问题，因为我们几乎一直与他们合作。所以我们就是这样逐步开展工作的，这也正是我们最初的需求所在——通过获取所需的洞察力来提升效率。（01:06:53）随后的情况是，Athenahealth当时的运作方式非常混乱且封闭。正因如此，我和许多高管同时离开了公司，但他们最终对公司进行了重组，保留了产品运营团队。如今，Tim Davenport负责监督产品运营团队。他曾是首席产品官的幕僚长，一直在不断完善团队，借鉴成功经验并在此基础上进行创新。Tim目前的做法以及他如何协调处理运营成本、资本支出和财务管理等问题，也成为我们书中重点研究的案例之一。（01:07:28）自从我离开后，Athenahealth经历了多次重组，但始终保留了产品运营团队。现任首席产品官表示，他绝不会去没有产品运营团队的公司工作。这足以说明他对产品运营团队的重视程度。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow. What a testament to the value of product ops, 100% retention on the role through all these transitions. One of the interesting things you said is within this VP of product ops managed a bunch of different people and teams, which is really interesting because I always imagine product ops VP would manage product ops people. Is that common where they lead, say, there's a data team you mentioned and a few other team?
turns.zh: 哇。产品运营的价值真是显而易见啊，在所有变动中，这个岗位的留存率达到了100%。你提到的有趣点是，产品运营副总裁要管理多个不同的人员和团队，这真的很有意思，因为我一直以为产品运营副总裁应该只负责产品运营团队。这种情况常见吗？比如说，你提到的数据团队，还有其他团队？

turns.speaker: Melissa Perri
turns.en: Yeah. In this case, we did have her managing the business data and insights people and they were data analysts. I wouldn't say they were data engineers or anything like that, but there were people who were really good at pulling SQL and analyzing data from a product perspective. We actually moved. I should say this as well. We moved a lot of people who didn't want to be product managers but were good at that out of the role and into that role. So they had some product background, they had been trained in product, they were really good at the data pieces, but they were more suited for that than they were suited for product management. Like I said, a lot of people opted out. They were like, "Get me out of this role. I don't want to do this." They wanted more of a transactional type role or diving into data, and a lot of it came down to I think people under anticipate how much they're going to have to deal with stakeholders, and once they have to, they're like, "Oh, God, I don't want to do this," and I see that over and over again when it happens with product management. (01:09:00): So she oversaw them, but they did work closely with the data people on the CTO side. There was a whole data team on the CTO side who were doing more of the database administration and the instrumentation of things. They were also helping to roll out Amplitude, instrument it correctly, and building the right views and things like Amplitudes or the other product analytics or other tools that they were using. We did not have Tableau at the time. That was something that was added later, but they were in charge of utilizing the data and trying to build those insights.
turns.zh: 是的。在我们公司，她确实负责管理商业数据和洞察团队，这些人都是数据分析师。我不会说他们是数据工程师之类的，但确实有一些人非常擅长从产品视角提取SQL数据并进行分析。实际上，我们还进行了调整。我也应该说明一下。我们把很多不愿做产品经理但又擅长这方面的人从产品经理岗位调到了这个角色。他们有产品背景，接受过产品培训，数据能力也不错，但相比产品管理，他们更适合这个角色。就像我说的，很多人选择退出。他们会说：“让我离开这个岗位吧。我不想做这个。”他们更想做交易型角色，或者深入研究数据。很多情况下，人们低估了需要与利益相关者打交道的难度，等真要面对时，就会说：“天哪，我不想做这个。” 我在产品管理领域反复看到这种情况。  (01:09:00)：所以她监督这些团队，但他们确实与CTO团队的数据人员密切合作。CTO团队有一个完整的数据团队，负责数据库管理和工具集成。他们还帮助部署Amplitude，正确配置Amplitude，构建合适的视图，以及使用Amplitude、其他产品分析工具或其他相关工具。当时我们没有Tableau，那是后来才添加的。但他们负责利用数据并试图构建洞察力。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. With that, we've reached our very exciting lightning round. I've never done this with two people. We'll see how it goes. So you can pick the question you want to take or both answer. Here we go. What are two or three books you've recommended most to other people?
turns.zh: 太棒了。说到这，我们迎来了一个非常激动人心的闪电问答环节。我从没和两个人一起做过这种环节。看看效果如何吧。你可以选择你想回答的问题，或者两个都回答。开始吧。你向其他人推荐最多的两三本书是什么？

turns.speaker: Denise Tilles
turns.en: I'll take that. Of course, Escaping the Build Trap. It's true.
turns.zh: 我来回答。当然，《逃离构建陷阱》。这本书说得很对。

turns.speaker: Melissa Perri
turns.en: I thought you would say that.
turns.zh: 我就知道你会这么说。

turns.speaker: Denise Tilles
turns.en: Another one that I recommend is called Traffic. It came out this year by Ben Smith, around the invention and growth of HuffPo and Gawker and whatnot. I was in media at Condé Nast then, so peripherally part of it. It's an exciting ride that has an ending that we all know, but it's a good story, good tale.
turns.zh: 我推荐的另一本书叫《流量》，本·史密斯今年出版的，讲的是HuffPo和Gawker等媒体的创立和发展。我当时在康泰纳仕做媒体工作，所以算是间接参与其中。这是一段激动人心的旅程，结局我们都知道，但故事很精彩。

turns.speaker: Melissa Perri
turns.en: The Art of Action I think is a fantastic book on strategy and I always recommend this to people and it's out of the realm. There's a lot of great product management books out there too, but I like this one because it's a sleeper hit, I think, in the product management community. It is a fantastic description of deploying strategy and how you can tell if strategy is well-deployed in organizations or if there's gaps that you need to fill. So I find that when people read it, they go, "Oh, my God, we have all of these problems," and I'm like, "Yup, that's a strategy deployment and strategy creation problem. That's pretty apparent." So that's my favorite book to recommend to people. I love Theresa Torres' Continuous Discovery Habits. Fantastic book as well, just to give a shout out in the product world too.
turns.zh: 我认为《行动的艺术》是一本关于战略的绝佳书籍，我总是向人们推荐它，它超出了人们的想象。市面上也有很多优秀的产品管理书籍，但我特别喜欢这本，因为它在产品管理领域堪称一匹黑马。我认为它出色地描述了如何部署战略，以及如何判断组织中的战略是否得到了有效实施，还是存在需要填补的空白。所以当人们读到它时，会感叹：“天哪，我们也存在这些问题。”而我会说：“没错，这就是战略部署和战略制定的问题，显而易见。”所以这是我最喜欢推荐给别人的书。我还很喜欢特蕾莎·托雷斯的《持续探索习惯》。这本书也很棒，我想在产品界也推荐一下。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Next question, favorite recent movie or TV show that you've really enjoyed?
turns.zh: 下一个问题，您最近有没有特别喜欢的电影或电视剧？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Like Pedal.
turns.zh: 比如《踏板》。

turns.speaker: Denise Tilles
turns.en: Yeah, really great.
turns.zh: 是的，真的很棒。

turns.speaker: Melissa Perri
turns.en: I am going to go ... I just watched the House of Usher on Netflix. I love the ... It's Halloween right now. Well, it was just Halloween.

turns.speaker: Denise Tilles
turns.en: Perfect.
turns.zh: 完美。

turns.speaker: Melissa Perri
turns.en: So I was watching all the scary movies, but I love the Netflix genre of everything from the Haunting of Hill House. Those were great.
turns.zh: 所以我一直在看各种恐怖片，但我最喜欢Netflix上从《鬼入侵》开始的所有类型片。那些都非常棒。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. I started watching that and then I gave up quickly, but I should give it another chance. My wife and I have been stuck on Love is Blind. Classic.
turns.zh: 太棒了。我开始看，但很快就放弃了，不过我应该再给它一次机会。我和妻子最近一直在追《爱情盲盒》。这部剧太经典了。

turns.speaker: Denise Tilles
turns.en: Same.

turns.en: Same.

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Next question, do you have a favorite interview question that you'd like to ask when you're hiring people?
turns.zh: 下一个问题，您在招聘时最喜欢问的面试问题是什么？

turns.speaker: Denise Tilles
turns.en: When was the last time you changed your mind about something really important and why? So do they have a learning mindset? Do they have self-awareness? Can they acknowledge where they were and how they evolved? So that's usually a pretty insightful question.
turns.zh: 您上一次改变对某件重要事情的看法是什么时候，为什么？这样就能判断他们是否有学习型思维吗？他们是否有自我意识？他们能承认自己的过去和成长吗？所以这通常是个很有洞察力的问题。

turns.speaker: Melissa Perri
turns.en: Mine's probably tell me about a time that you failed and what happened. That one's an interesting one too because if nobody has an example of a time that they failed, that right there is an interesting sign. Two, I feel like everybody tries to turn it into a positive story. They really try to spin it and I'm like, "I don't even want you to spin it. I just want to tell me what you learned." It's fine to say what you learned at the end of that. I think that's okay, but they're like, "Oh, but this happened and all these things were great afterwards," and I'm like, "I'm not looking for a fantastic outcome. I'm just looking for did you fail and did you learn something from it."
turns.zh: 我最喜欢的可能是让他们讲一次自己失败的经历以及结果。这是个很有趣的问题，因为如果没人能举出失败的例子，那本身就是个值得注意的信号。其次，我觉得每个人都会试图把它包装成一个积极的故事。他们总想粉饰太平，而我会说：“我不想听你美化它，我只想知道你从中学到了什么。”你可以在最后再说学到了什么。我觉得这没问题，但他们会说：“哦，但后来发生了这些事，结果都很棒。”而我会说：“我不关心结果，我只想知道你有没有失败，有没有从中吸取教训。”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Do you have a favorite product you've recently discovered that you really like?
turns.zh: 您最近有没有发现特别喜欢的产品？

turns.speaker: Melissa Perri
turns.en: Well, there's one I'm going to have to plug. It's not that I recently discovered it, but I talked about all the issues that we had at Athenahealth with the portfolio management system, and after that, I discovered Dragon Boat and I'm now on their advisory board, but it helped me solve that problem. So much of rolling up everything that was in Jira sits on top of it and being able to look at it in a great view. So that was so, so good. (01:13:13): Another one that I have not been involved with but that I just really love because I think they're doing great things with, again, in the product ops world, is Dovetail and they are a research repository out there and they're also putting AI on top of it to help generate insights into all the research that's been done. I have no affiliation with Dovetail, but I really love what they're doing because I've had that problem of us rolling our own research repository over and over and over again, and now we've got a tool out there to do it.
turns.zh: 嗯，有一个我得推荐一下。虽然我最近才发现它，但之前我谈到了Athenahealth在投资组合管理系统方面遇到的种种问题。在那之后，我接触到了Dragon Boat，现在我成了他们的顾问委员会成员，但它确实帮我解决了那个问题。把Jira里所有内容整合起来的功能非常棒，能以直观的视角查看所有信息。这真是太棒了。（01:13:13）：另一个我没参与过但非常欣赏的公司是Dovetail。他们在产品运营领域做得很棒，是一家研究库平台，还在其基础上应用了人工智能，帮助人们从已有研究中提取洞见。我和Dovetail没有合作关系，但我真的很欣赏他们的工作，因为我们曾反复尝试自己搭建研究库，现在终于有了一个现成的工具可以解决这个问题。

turns.speaker: Denise Tilles
turns.en: I guess the one I would mention is Vistali, and some product leaders that I'm working with right now are playing around with it, and it's an interesting tool that's a single workspace that you can connect your strategy and discovery and delivery visually and guides people along those paths as well. So interested to play with it more, but it piqued my interest.
turns.zh: 我想提到的还有Vistali，我现在合作的一些产品负责人正在试用它。这是个很有趣的工具，提供了一个单一的工作空间，你可以直观地连接战略、发现和交付路径，还能沿着这些路径引导团队。很期待能更深入地探索它，但它确实引起了我的兴趣。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Do you have a favorite life motto that you often repeat to yourself, often share with someone, come back to often to help either with work or with life?
turns.zh: 你有没有经常对自己重复、经常与人分享、经常回味以帮助工作或生活的心灵鸡汤？

turns.speaker: Denise Tilles
turns.en: Mine's both, especially with teams that I'm working with or cross-functional stakeholders that if you try to serve everybody, you serve no one. So it's about honing in on who you're actually building your product for, who your persona is, and then with my children in terms of try to be everyone's friend, but it may not happen. So it goes both ways.
turns.zh: 我两者都有，特别是对于合作的团队或跨职能的利益相关者来说，如果你试图取悦所有人，就等于取悦不了任何人。所以关键在于明确产品真正为谁服务，了解你的用户画像。对我和孩子相处时，比如想成为每个人的朋友，但可能做不到。所以这两者是相通的。

turns.speaker: Melissa Perri
turns.en: What's the worst that can happen with most of the things that I've done? To me when I get scared about something or trying to do something or even interpersonal reactions where I'm like, "God, I have to have this hard conversation with this person," my brain, I try to tell myself, "What's the worst that can happen?" Usually when you sit down and start to think about it, it's not as bad as you anticipate. So for me, that's always helped me manage my anxiety around difficult situations or taking a leap and trying to get out there. I think in my younger days, I was a little crippled by overthinking and by being too anxious about things and not taking big leaps. So I've tried to stick by that and keep asking myself, "What's the worst that can happen?" and it's usually not as bad as you think it is.
turns.zh: 我做过的大多数事情，最坏的情况会怎样？对我来说，当我对某件事感到恐惧，或者尝试做某件事时，甚至在人际交往中遇到需要严肃对话的局面时，我的大脑会提醒自己：“最坏的情况会怎样？”通常当你静下心来思考时，情况并没有你预想的那么糟糕。所以对我来说，这一直帮助我应对困难局面时的焦虑，或者勇敢尝试新事物。回想年轻时，我曾因过度思考、过度焦虑而裹足不前，错失良机。所以我一直努力秉持这个理念，不断问自己：“最坏的情况会怎样？”，结果往往比你想象的要好得多。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that. Final question, since there's two of you, we'll end in a really sweet way. What's one thing you really admire about each other?
turns.zh: 我喜欢这个问题。最后一个问题，因为你们两人都在场，我们会以一个温馨的方式结束。你们最欣赏对方的哪一点？

turns.speaker: Denise Tilles
turns.en: Melissa is a legend, but behind the legend, she's just a really great collaborative person. So of course, we got to know each other really well writing this book together. We worked together before that, but it was a really great way of staying connected to a former colleague, someone in the industry. Especially during COVID, it was a really great way of building towards something that was bigger than the both of us. So what I love about her is that she's really revered by so many folks, but really approachable and really truly wants to help people.
turns.zh: 梅丽莎是个传奇人物，但在传奇背后，她其实是个非常善于合作的人。所以在共同撰写这本书的过程中，我们彼此熟悉得非常快。之前我们也曾合作过，但这次合作是保持与前同事、业内人士联系的绝佳方式。尤其是在新冠疫情期间，这为我们共同打造比个人更宏大的事业提供了宝贵契机。让我欣赏她的地方在于，她备受尊崇却又平易近人，真心愿意帮助他人。

turns.speaker: Melissa Perri
turns.en: Thanks, Denise. What I love about Denise is she's really this calming, patient presence and she approaches everything with so much professionalism, but also can really get to the meat of the problem, help calm down certain situations where escalated, turn them around, and she's got this patience and calm about her in everything that she does that helps you focus, helps you concentrate on the big issues and she can really steer people in the right direction. So to me, I've always admired watching her coach and lead people. She led her analysts at Produx Labs as well. When things would go slightly awry or a situation would go out of hand, Denise was always like, "Nope, we'll just fix it," and dove in and was able to make it better. I always really appreciated that.
turns.zh: 谢谢你，丹妮丝。我欣赏她的是，她总能带来令人安心的耐心与专业精神。她处理问题时务实高效，能迅速切中要害，化解紧张局势。她做事时始终保持冷静，让人专注于核心问题，能引导他人朝着正确方向前进。我一直很钦佩她指导和领导团队的能力。她在Produx Labs也出色地领导过分析师团队。当事情稍有偏差或局面失控时，丹妮丝总会说：“没关系，我们能解决。”然后亲自介入，扭转局面。我对此深感赞赏。

turns.speaker: Denise Tilles
turns.en: Oh, shocks. We might've had a few of the what's the worst that could happen moments, right?
turns.zh: 哦，天哪。我们可能也经历过不少“最坏情况会怎样”的时刻，对吧？

turns.speaker: Melissa Perri
turns.en: Always.
turns.zh: 每次都是。

turns.en: Amazing. You two are awesome. For folks listening, make sure to grab their book, Product Operations. You can find it on Amazon, I imagine. Share where else people can find it, but two final questions. Where can folks find you online if they want to reach out and how can listeners be useful to you?

turns.en: Productoperations.com, we've got some downloadables that are available for folks and questions if you want to get in touch with us. How can they help us? I'm trying to think here.
turns.zh: Productoperations.com，我们为读者准备了下载资源。还有问题的话随时联系我们。你们如何能帮助我们？我现在在想。

turns.speaker: Melissa Perri
turns.en: Tell us your stories about product operations. We want to hear how people are implementing it, what's working, what's not working. We're always learning about this too, and I think we said in this book, it's ticking off now, but it's by no means standardized. So we want to hear about what's happening, how has your company been successful or not successful with it, what have you seen work, what have you seen not work. So definitely reach out and let us know about it. Also, you can help us by buying the book and leaving us an Amazon review if you do read it because that does help authors and we self-publish this one too, so that always helps us on there. (01:18:17): You can find both of us on LinkedIn as well. I'm Melissa Jean Perri, I think on, there, but if you look for Melissa Perri, I usually pop up and Denise Tilles. Then if you want to contact us, product operations.com, we got a form on there to reach out.
turns.zh: 请和我们分享你们在产品运营方面的故事。我们想听听大家是如何实施的，哪些方法有效，哪些无效。我们自己也在不断学习，正如我们在书中所说，虽然产品运营正在推进，但远未形成标准化。因此，我们希望听到大家的实践经验，看看你们的公司是如何成功或失败的，哪些方法有效，哪些无效。所以一定要联系我们，让我们了解你们的做法。另外，买了书的朋友可以在亚马逊上给我们写评价，这对作者很有帮助，我们这本书也是自出版的，这对我们在平台上的推广也很有帮助。（01:18:17）你们也可以在LinkedIn上找到我们。我是梅丽莎·简·佩里，我想在那里能找到我，但如果你们搜梅丽莎·佩里，我通常会出现，还有丹妮丝·蒂尔斯。想联系我们的话，可以访问productoperations.com，我们在那里设有联系表单。

turns.en: Productoperations.com. Is that the best way to find where to buy the book or are there other sites you recommend people go check it out?
turns.zh: Productoperations.com。这是购买书籍的最佳途径吗？还是有其他推荐的购买渠道？

turns.en: We do. We just got it. Self-publishing has been fun, but we just got it where it is distributing now to Barnes and Noble and other bookstores. Then if you go to your bookstore and some people are against Amazon, so if you go to your bookstore and ask for it, they will be able to order it for you.
turns.zh: 是的，我们确实做到了。我们刚刚完成了相关工作。自助出版的过程很有趣，但现在我们的书已经开始在巴诺书店等实体书店上架了。所以你通常能在各大平台上找到它，但如果你访问我们的官网，里面会提供最新的销售信息。另外，有些人可能反感亚马逊平台，所以如果你去书店询问，他们会帮你下单购买。

turns.en: Amazing. Thank you two for being here.
